To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Bax/Bax and MPTP are both required for cell death mediated by necroptosis.
Bax/Bax and cyclophilin-D (Ppif) are required for cell death induced by the necroptotic pathway and that this cell death requires MOMP and MPTP opening and is mediated by MLKL, cofilin- and Mcl-1.
Bax and Bax/Bak are required for necrooptosis, and that this cell death pathway involves mitochondrial outer membrane permeablization and MPTP opening.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the mechanisms of cell death and the regulation of cell death pathways by the mitochondrial death pathway.
the molecular mechanisms of cell death and how these mechanisms can be manipulated to prevent or treat disease.
the regulation of mitochondrial outer membrane permeability and the interface between apoptosis and necroptosis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Bax and/or Bak are not only required for apoptosis but also for necroptosis.
necroptosis interfaces with MOMP and MPTP to induce cell death.
the BCL-2 family members and the cyclophilin-D mediated mitochondrial permeability transition (MPT) are both required for cell death induced by the necroptotic pathway.

Bax/Bax and RIPK3 are both required for necroptic cell death and that Bax/Bac and RIPK3 function together in this cell death pathway.
